You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 1a, which of the following best describes the location and characteristics of the cavitary lesion, and what is the most likely diagnosis considering the clinical context provided?

A) Right middle zone cavitary lesion with thick walls, no linear tracks; likely pulmonary tuberculosis.
B) Right middle zone cavitary lesion with thin walls, associated with a linear track; likely pulmonary Paragonimiasis.
C) Left upper zone cavitary lesion with thin walls, no linear tracks; likely lung carcinoma.
D) Right lower zone cavitary lesion with thick walls, associated with a linear track; likely pulmonary abscess.
E) Bilateral upper zone cavitary lesions with thin walls, no linear tracks; likely pulmonary aspergillosis.
F) Right upper zone cavitary lesion with thin walls, associated with a curvilinear track; likely pulmonary Paragonimiasis.
